transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess it’s because of some things I’ve been doing at church. People notice. Like at the potluck, I’ll just stand there holding the serving spoon up and not move. Or I keep folding the same napkins again and again while folks are waiting. It’s… odd, I know.
Do you feel upset or bothered by these things you've been doing at church?
I don’t know… not really upset, I guess. It’s more embarrassing when people look at me. I try not to think on it too much.
Do you feel like you have to perform these actions, like holding the serving spoon or folding the napkins, or can you stop yourself if you want to?

I… I don’t know if I have to. I just sort of end up doing it, like standing there with the spoon, or folding those napkins again. I can stop if someone says something, but on my own I don’t always seem to.
Do you feel like these actions, such as holding the spoon or folding napkins, are something you need to do in order to prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t noticed it being about stopping something bad. It just kind of happens, and I don’t always know why.
Do you feel like you're doing these actions, like holding the spoon or folding napkins, over and over because you feel compelled to do them perfectly?
No… I don’t think it’s about doing it perfect. I just get stuck doing it, like holding the serving spoon there or folding the same napkins again, and people are waiting. I don’t really know why.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind that you can't get rid of?
I’m not sure… not really like that, I don’t think. I don’t notice thoughts repeating over and over.
Do you feel like you have to follow a specific routine or ritual when performing daily tasks?
I don’t think I have a routine like that… not one I’m aware of. I just do things, I guess.
Do you feel anxious when you're unable to perform these repetitive actions, like holding the spoon or folding the napkins?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say anxious. Maybe I get a little bothered if someone stops me, but I haven’t really noticed feeling scared or anything like that.
Do you feel like you are being driven to do these repetitive actions, like holding the spoon or folding the napkins?

I don’t know if I’d say driven… it just sort of happens. At church I’ll be by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just not move, or I’ll keep folding the same napkins while people are waiting. I don’t really mean to make trouble.
Do you feel like there are other actions or behaviors besides holding the spoon or folding napkins that you feel compelled to repeat?
Mostly just those things at church… the spoon, and the napkins. I can’t think of much else right now. It’s just odd things like that, and people end up waiting on me.
Do you feel more comfortable or less tense when you're doing these repetitive actions, like holding the spoon or folding the napkins?
Maybe a little… I don’t really know. When I’m holding the spoon or folding the napkins, I’m just doing it. I’m not thinking much. People are waiting, and then I realize it’s odd.
How do you feel when someone interrupts you while you're doing something like holding the spoon or folding the napkins?
I guess I feel a little embarrassed when they interrupt me. Like I didn’t notice I was holding up the spoon or messing with the napkins again. I usually just stop and feel kind of awkward.
Do you feel distressed when you think about the repetitive things you've been doing?
A little, yes. Mostly I feel embarrassed thinking about it… standing there at church with the spoon, or folding napkins again while people are waiting. It bothers me because I don’t mean to do it.
Do you think these behaviors, like holding the spoon or folding napkins, are interfering with your daily life or relationships?

A little, I think. I’ve had to step back from some things at choir and church… volunteering and such. I get mixed up with plans sometimes, and then people get uncomfortable or have to fix what I was supposed to do. So… yes, I suppose it has.
Do you feel like the way you're doing things, like folding the napkins, needs to be a certain way or look a certain way?
I don’t know… I don’t think it has to look a certain way. I just sort of do it, and then notice after.
Do you feel like doing these repetitive actions helps you feel less anxious or worried?
I don’t think it really helps with worry. It’s more like… I just find myself doing it. Like at church, with the spoon, or the napkins. I’m not trying to calm myself, exactly.
Do you feel like the things you repeat, like folding the napkins, have to be symmetrical or exact in some way?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really noticed it needing to be exact. I just do it, I suppose.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, thoughts come and go, but I haven’t noticed anything like that bothering me over and over.
Do you have thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress, but they keep coming back to you?
No… I don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed. I don’t really try to push thoughts away like that.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and bother you?
No… I can’t say I have that. Nothing that keeps going around and bothering me, not really.
